docs.title: Sojourn documentation
docs.text: Sojourn is in development. These pages cover what is in the package today and grow with every sprint.

docs.title: Start here: three steps to your first report, about 25 minutes
docs.text:
1. Install Sojourn About 10 minutesInstall the package in a sandbox or production org and open the Sojourn app.
  2. Assign permission sets About 5 minutesGive admins, managers, and everyone else the access Sojourn needs.
  3. Track Cases and open your first report About 10 minutesTurn on tracking for Case status and owner, then open the Time in Status by Case report.

docs.title: New here?
docs.text:
Sojourn records how long every record spends in each status and with each owner, in business hours, as plain rows you can report on. Each Tracked field gets its own lane.

Sample data. The Coral part of the Status lane is time past the Goal.

docs.title: Sprint 8: Free and Plus plans, hardening, and performance runs (18 October 2026)
docs.text:
• Free and Plus plans. Sojourn installs on the Free plan: tracking Case, Lead, and Opportunity, the record timeline, the reports and dashboards, goals and breach flags, business hours, pause and Catch up, summaries, the Health Monitor, and settings export and import. The Plus plan adds tracking for any other object, Live values on the record, Backfill with History or Seed, purge and the archive, and Omni-Channel agent work. On Free, Plus features stay visible in Sojourn Settings with their controls off and an Upgrade to Plus link. Moving an org from Plus to Free deletes nothing. See Free and Plus plans.
  • New guide pages: Check the prerequisites, Track Cases and open your first report, Run the jobs, Troubleshooting, and Uninstall Sojourn. The install guide gains the upgrade steps, and Assign permission sets explains that Intervals are Public Read Only and how to make them Private.
  • Checks on every change: every Sojourn screen method checks a Sojourn permission before it reads or writes, production code has no test-only switches, no record Id is written into code or metadata, and only the ChangeCapture entry point is global.
  • Performance: 2,000 Cases loaded through Bulk API 2.0 with Status and owner tracked cost Sojourn about 400 ms of CPU per 200-record chunk, and summaries, reconcile, and purge were timed on 72,003 Intervals. The results are in Reports at large volume.

docs.title: Sprint 7: the record timeline, reports, and dashboards (14 October 2026)
docs.text:
• The Sojourn Timeline on record pages and Experience Cloud pages: a lane per Tracked field, each stay sized by its time, goal ticks and the time past a goal, details on focus or hover, and totals by value and by owner. History purged to the archive shows too, marked as archived.
  • The Sojourn Timeline permission, in the Sojourn User, Manager, Health Monitor, and Admin permission sets, and a new Sojourn Site User permission set for Experience Cloud users. The timeline shows the history of a record only to people who can open the record.
  • 20 reports in the Sojourn Reports folder and 4 dashboards in Sojourn Dashboards: Desk Productivity, Process Bottlenecks, SLA Health, and Leaderboards. Trends and leaderboards read the daily summaries, so they stay fast at any volume.
  • The report cookbook gains worked examples, hours per Case, status groups, and reports at large volume, and the reference lists every report and dashboard with the filters it relies on.
  • Live values, goals, and capture use the same status field as the Case metrics when an object has none chosen.

docs.title: Sprint 6: Case metrics, Omni-Channel, and breach alerts (13 October 2026)
docs.text:
• Case metrics on every Case: first closed at, business minutes to first close, reopens, owner and status changes, and business minutes held by queues, by agents, and in total. They are rebuilt from the Case's own Intervals whoever saves the Case, and by Backfill and repair.
  • The Sojourn Omni-Channel package: one Agent work Interval per agent assignment of routed work, closed with its minutes when the work ends. It installs only in orgs with Omni-Channel; the core package does not need it.
  • The Sojourn Breach Alert Template Flow: save a copy, activate it, and the Interval owner and their manager get one email when an Interval breaches its goal.
  • The Case Status At Close field on Intervals is removed before the first release.
  • The purge runs list shows how many files each run saved, and a stopped run shows what it deleted before it stopped.

docs.title: Sprint 5: summaries, retention, goals, and moving settings (12 October 2026)
docs.text:
• Summaries each night: closed Intervals counted into daily and monthly rows, kept when Intervals are purged, with the Sojourn Interval Summaries report type and Rebuild summaries for whole months.
  • Retention and purge: choose Keep everything or Keep a number of days. A purge deletes only closed, summarised Intervals older than the window, saves each part to a CSV file on its purge run first, and can copy them to the archive. Purge now runs one straight away; both ask you to type DELETE.
  • Goals per value of a Tracked field, in business minutes, with a warn-at percent.
  • Business hours per queue, so time owned by a queue counts in that queue's hours.
  • Export settings to a file and import it in another org, with a check of what will change before Apply, and Replace what is here to match the file.
  • At most 10 Tracked fields per object, Start timing at the first value for fields that start blank, and an Estimate of the Interval rows and storage your choice adds.
  • The Sojourn app has three tabs: Sojourn Settings, Health Monitor, and Intervals.
  • The Health Monitor shows a Flow you cannot see as information rather than a warning, and a catch up keeps its window when capture was paused during the run.

docs.title: Sprint 4: jobs and the Health Monitor (12 October 2026)
docs.text:
• Backfill from an object's screen: History builds past Intervals from field history, Seed starts each record from its current values, and Fresh starts with the next change. The card shows Queued, Running, Complete, or Failed with what was done.
  • Catch up after a pause: the records changed while capture was paused get their Intervals at the time they changed, and running it again is safe.
  • Live values: minutes to date and breach flags on open Intervals, and the minute fields on each record, every 10, 15, 20, 30, or 60 minutes.
  • Reconcile each night: flags Intervals of deleted or merged records, repairs drift from the record's current values, and retries Limit and DML errors.
  • A Jobs card on the Sojourn Settings overview to turn Live values and Reconcile on, change their schedule, and see the last and next run.
  • The Health Monitor tab: overall health, capture checks, job runs, error counts, and an error list with Create Interval, Ignore, and Mark resolved, each error with what happened, why, and how to fix it.
  • The Sojourn Health Monitor permission set, so a support or operations group can fix errors without Sojourn Settings.
  • Tracking errors are now the Error Log, with a Create Interval action on each record.
  • The Sojourn Settings screens match the approved designs, and the Tracked objects list shows each object's Tracked fields, Track owner, and where its business hours come from.

  • Pause and Resume capture per object, with the time the pause started.
  • A capture status for every Tracked object: Tracked by package, Flow active, Flow missing, or Flow unknown, with Re-check.
  • The Sojourn Capture Template Flow and four steps on screen to turn on capture for any other object.
  • Org-wide Tracking enabled and default business hours, saved with Save settings.
  • Shorter API names: the namespace already names the package, so components no longer repeat it.

docs.text:

docs.title: Report cookbook
docs.text: Tell us the report you need and we will write it up first.

docs.title: Filter by object, then field, then value
docs.text:
Every interval belongs to one Tracked object and one Tracked field. Before you group by Value, filter or group by Tracked object and then Tracked field. A grouping that mixes fields adds Status minutes to Owner minutes, and the totals stop meaning anything.

The 19 packaged reports (20 with Sojourn Omni-Channel) and 4 dashboards, with the filters each relies on, are listed in Reports and dashboards. They follow this rule: each filters Tracked Field before it groups by value. The dashboards run as the user each one names, the installing admin until you change it; see step 3 of Install Sojourn before you share them.

  • Worked examples: time in status for a queue, time per owner, and the statuses that miss their goal.
  • Hours per Case: total business hours, from the Case metrics or from the Intervals.
  • Status groups: edit the bucket that splits customer time from company time.
  • Reports at large volume: date ranges, custom indexes, and summaries for trends.

docs.title: Report on summaries
docs.text:
Summary rows keep the totals after Intervals are purged; see Keep or purge Intervals. Use the Sojourn Interval Summaries report type.

  1. Filter Granularity to Month for trends, or Day for the last weeks. Never add Day and Month rows together: each Month row already holds its days.
  2. Filter Parent Object and Tracked Field, as for Intervals, then group by To Value, and by Owner Name for time per owner.
  3. For the average time in a value, add a summary formula: the sum of Sum Business Minutes divided by the sum of Interval Count. Averaging Avg Business Minutes across rows weighs a quiet day like a busy one.
  4. Breach Count counts the Intervals that ran past their goal.

Record Count is close, not exact. It counts each record once per row as the row is built. A record that gets another Interval later for a period already summarised is counted again on that row, so the count can run slightly high. Interval Count and the minutes are exact.

docs.title: From the Case metrics
docs.text:
Every Case carries Sojourn Total Business Minutes: the business minutes it spent with finished owners, queues and users together. See Read the Case metrics.

  1. Create a report on the standard Cases report type.
  2. Add Sojourn Total Business Minutes, Sojourn Queue Business Minutes, and Sojourn Agent Business Minutes.
  3. For hours, add a summary formula: the sum of Sojourn Total Business Minutes divided by 60.

The time with the current owner is not in these totals until the owner changes; it is in Sojourn Owner Minutes while Live values run.

docs.title: From the Intervals
docs.text:
1. Open Time in Status by Case and Save As.
  2. Remove the grouping by To Value, so each Case shows one line.
  3. Elapsed Business Hours summed per Case is the time in every status, the current one up to its last Live values refresh.

Use one way per report: the two count the current stay differently.

docs.title: Reports at large volume
docs.text:
An org that tracks several fields on busy objects writes Intervals quickly. These habits keep reports fast.

  1. Filter on a date range of Entered At. Every Interval report should limit Entered At, or the report's own date, to the weeks you need. The packaged averages already look back 30 or 90 days.
  2. Ask Salesforce Support for custom indexes on Entered_At__c, Tracked_Field__c, and Parent_Object__c of Sojourn Intervals once the object passes a few million rows. Support adds custom indexes on request.
  3. Use the daily summaries for trends. Average Hours per Status by Week and Owner Leaderboard, Last 30 Days read the Interval Summaries, one row per day, value, and owner, so they stay fast at any volume. The packaged dashboards' trend and leaderboard charts read only these. See Report on summaries.
  4. Keep detail off on large groupings. Summary reports with Show Details off return totals without every row.

Often missed. Purging old Intervals keeps the summaries. Trends built on summaries survive a purge; reports on Intervals show only what is left. See Keep or purge Intervals.

docs.title: What we measured
docs.text:
A scratch org holding 6,000 Cases and 72,003 Intervals spread over 400 days, on the Plus plan, gave these times in sprint 8:

Step Result The 19 Sojourn reports All ran; the slowest took 4 seconds, the rest 1 second or less Summaries 72,003 Intervals counted in 81 seconds Reconcile 7 seconds Purge, keeping 30 days 57,715 Intervals saved to CSV files and deleted in 231 seconds, no errors

Loading 2,000 Cases through Bulk API 2.0 with Status and owner tracked cost Sojourn about 400 ms of CPU per 200-record chunk; each chunk's whole save stayed under 600 ms. A scratch org holds far fewer Intervals than a production org, so the same steps run again at millions of Intervals in a sandbox before Sojourn is listed on AppExchange.

docs.title: Status groups
docs.text:
Share of Time per Status Group sums business minutes per status group: time waiting on the customer against time with your company. The package cannot know your status values, so the report ships with example values in a bucket field named Status group:

Group Example statuses Customer Waiting on Customer Company New, Working, Escalated Other Every status not listed

docs.title: Edit the bucket
docs.text:
1. Open Share of Time per Status Group and select Save As into your folder.
  2. In the report builder, open the Status group column's menu and select Edit Bucket Column.
  3. Move each of your statuses into Customer or Company, add groups if you need them, and save.

A report has at most 5 bucket fields, 20 buckets per field, and 20 values per bucket.

docs.title: Worked examples
docs.text: Each example starts from a packaged report in Sojourn Reports. Packaged reports are read only: select Save As to keep your changes in your own folder. The sample results below come from a demo org.

docs.title: Where did this queue's Cases spend their time this month?
docs.text:
1. Open Time in Status by Case, then Save As into your folder.
  2. In Filters, add Case Owner equals your queue, and set the date range to This Month on Date/Time Opened.
  3. Keep the filter Tracked Field equals Status: it is what keeps Status time apart from Owner time.

docs.title: Who held a Case, and for how long?
docs.text:
1. Open Time per Owner by Case.
  2. Filter Case Number to the Case, or keep every Case and sort by Elapsed Business Hours.
  3. Queues and users both appear; a queue's time counts in that queue's business hours (see Set goals and business hours).

docs.text:
1. Open SLA Breaches by Status and Owner. It lists every stay that went past its Goal, by value and then owner.
  2. To see one object, add Parent Object equals Case.
  3. Breaches are flagged by the Live values job; see Track an object.

docs.title: Backfill past Intervals
docs.text: A new Tracked object starts with the next change. Backfill gives the records that already exist their Intervals, so reports cover the time before you turned tracking on.

docs.title: Choose a mode
docs.text:
Open Sojourn Settings, then Tracked objects, then the object. The Backfill card offers three modes:

  • History recreates past Intervals from the object's field history: from each record's creation to its first change, then each change to the next, with the last one open. A Tracked field without history starts from its current value.
  • Seed starts each record from its current value: one open Interval per Tracked field, from the record's last change; the owner's Interval starts at the record's creation.
  • Fresh adds nothing: capture begins with the next change.

History and Seed are on the Plus plan; on the Free plan the card offers Fresh. See Free and Plus plans.

History needs field history tracking turned on for the object and its fields in Salesforce Setup before the changes happened. If the object keeps no field history at all, History seeds every record and says so in the result.

docs.title: Run it
docs.text:
1. Choose the mode, then Run backfill.
  2. Read the confirmation: it names the mode and the object. Choose Run backfill again.
  3. History and Seed run in the background, History 20 records at a time and Seed 200, because History reads every field change of each record. If the org leaves the Plus plan during a run, the run stops at its next part and shows Failed, saying how many records it reached; run it again on Plus to finish. A Queued or Running backfill with no job left going, for example after the object stopped being tracked, also shows Failed and says it stopped before it finished. The card shows Queued, then Running, then Complete or Failed with what was done, for example "Seed backfill on 12 Oct 2026, 13:56: 60 Intervals for 20 records." A new backfill is refused only while a backfill job is really running in the org (on any object), with "A backfill is still running. Try again when it finishes." If a run stopped before it could record its result, the card can still say Queued or Running; once no backfill job is going, you can run it again.

The job runs as you: only records and fields you can see are read and written. A backfill and a Catch up never run at the same time: each waits for the other to finish, so their parts cannot both open an Interval for the same field.

Safe to run again. Records and fields that already have Intervals are skipped, so a second run adds nothing to them. After a Failed run, run it again to finish the rest; the Error Log lists the part that failed.

You are done when

  • The Backfill card reads Complete.
  • An Interval report on the object shows Intervals that start before you added it.

docs.title: Email a breach alert
docs.text: When an Interval runs past its goal, Sojourn marks it as breached: the Live values job marks an Interval that is still open, and a stay that closes past its goal before the job saw it is marked when it closes. The Sojourn Breach Alert Template Flow turns that moment into an email to the Interval's owner and, when they have one in Salesforce, their manager. It ships inactive, so nothing is sent until you choose to.

docs.title: Turn it on
docs.text:
1. In Setup, open Flows, then Sojourn Breach Alert Template, and choose Save As, a new Flow.
  2. Change the subject and the body if you like. They name the record, the Tracked field, the value, the goal, and the business minutes so far.
  3. Activate your copy.

docs.title: Good to know
docs.text:
• For an open Interval, the alert fires inside the Live values job, which sets the breach. Turn on Live values on the Tracked object's screen and schedule the Live values job on the Sojourn Settings overview; without both, open Intervals are not marked breached and no alert is sent for them.
  • By default the template emails only while an Interval is still open, when someone can still act. To email for a stay that closed past its goal too, turn on Also email when a stay closes past its goal under Breach alerts on the Goals screen of Sojourn Settings. The setting applies to every Tracked object; the breach flag and reports are the same either way.
  • Only Intervals owned by a user are alerted. Queue-owned Intervals have no user to email.
  • Each email counts toward the org's daily email limit. If an email cannot be sent, the Flow ends without it and the save that marked the breach carries on.
  • Your copy is yours to change: add a condition on the Tracked field, or send to a team address instead.

You are done when

  • An Interval owned by you passes its goal and, after the next Live values run, you receive the alert.

docs.title: Read the Case metrics
docs.text: Once Case is a Tracked object with Status tracked, and Track owner on for the owner figures, every Case carries eight figures that Sojourn keeps from the Case's own Intervals.

docs.title: The fields
docs.text:
Field What it holds Sojourn First Closed At When the Case first entered a closed status. Reopening does not change it. Sojourn First Close Business Minutes Business minutes in every status before that first close. Sojourn Reopen Count Times the Case moved from a closed status back to an open one. Sojourn Status Change Count Status changes after creation: the Case's Status Intervals minus one. Sojourn Owner Change Count Handoffs between owners: the Owner Intervals minus one. A Case never reassigned shows 0. Sojourn Queue Business Minutes Business minutes the Case spent owned by queues. Sojourn Agent Business Minutes Business minutes the Case spent owned by users. Sojourn Total Business Minutes Queue and agent minutes together.

The queue, agent, and total minutes count finished ownership only. Time with the current owner is in Sojourn Owner Minutes, which the Live values job keeps current on the Plus plan (see Track an object).

A status is closed when it is in the Tracked object's Closed values. With Closed values empty and Status as the status field, Sojourn uses the case statuses marked Closed in Setup. If you track a custom status field, list its closed values; otherwise no value counts as closed and the first-close figures stay blank.

docs.title: When they change
docs.text:
Sojourn recomputes the figures from the Case's Status and Owner Intervals whenever one of them opens or closes: on every save, and after a catch up, a backfill, or a repair. A Case that missed an update, for example because a save was close to a Salesforce limit, is corrected by its next change.

Every Case gets its figures whoever saves it: Sojourn writes them itself, so agents do not need edit access to these fields, and the fields stay read-only for everyone but Sojourn admins. A catch up, backfill, repair, or the nightly Reconcile writes the figures in its own run, so the Case's Last Modified Date moves to that run's time.

docs.title: Sojourn's own update of the Case
docs.text:
Sojourn writes the figures with one more update of the Case, in the same transaction, right after a save that opens a Status or Owner Interval and after a Case is created. That update carries only the eight Sojourn fields, but your own Case automation runs for it like for any update: validation rules, before-update triggers, and Flows or processes set to run every time a record is edited. Set automation that should run once per user save to run only when the fields it cares about change.

If automation that runs during Sojourn's update changes the Case's Status or Owner, Sojourn records that change as it happens, like any other save, and recomputes the figures, unless a validation rule refuses Sojourn's update of another Case in the same save; then the next change to the Case or the Reconcile job records it. A validation rule that refuses Sojourn's update leaves the user's save in place; the refused figures are an entry in the Error Log, and the next change to the Case recomputes them.

Often missed. The figures are fields on Case, so they show only where you add them. Add them to your Case page layouts and to Case reports; Sojourn does not change your layouts.

docs.title: Add them to a Case page
docs.text:
1. In Setup, open Object Manager, then Case, then Page Layouts, and choose your layout.
  2. Drag the Sojourn fields into a section, for example one named Service metrics, and save.

You are done when

  • Closing a Case shows Sojourn First Closed At and its business minutes on the Case page.

docs.title: Set goals and business hours
docs.text: A goal says how long a record should stay in a value. Business hours say which minutes count. Both are set in Sojourn Settings, under Time.

docs.title: Set goals
docs.text:
Open Goals. Choose the Tracked object and the Tracked field; the field starts on the object's status field. Each value of the field has a row, with Any value first:

  • Target, business minutes: how long an Interval in this value should last. Leave it blank for no goal.
  • Warn at, percent: when the Health Monitor and reports show an Interval as close to its goal, from 1 to 100.

A value's own goal wins over Any value. Choose Save goals. New Intervals carry the goal; Intervals already open keep the one they started with. An Interval that runs past its goal is a Breach: the Live values job flags one that is still open, and a stay is flagged when it closes past its goal.

The Breach alerts card below the goals is for every Tracked object. Its switch, Also email when a stay closes past its goal, decides whether the breach alert email also goes for stays that closed late, or only while an Interval is still open (the default). See Email a breach alert; the card's When to turn it on explains the choice.

Clearing a target turns the goal off. Goals are never deleted, so Intervals that point at one keep it.

docs.title: Give queues their business hours
docs.text:
Open Business hours. The card at the top names the org default, the hours used when nothing more specific applies; change it on the Overview. The Queues table lists every queue with the objects it takes. Choose business hours for a queue, or leave it on Use the next rule, then choose Save.

For each Interval, Sojourn uses the first of these that is set:

  1. The Tracked field's own business hours.
  2. A business hours field on the record, when the Tracked object names one.
  3. The queue's business hours, while a queue owns the record.
  4. The Tracked object's business hours.
  5. The Sojourn default on the Overview, then the org's default business hours.

Changes apply to Intervals that start after you save.

You are done when

  • An Interval created after you save shows the goal on its record.
  • An Interval for a record owned by a mapped queue counts business minutes in that queue's hours.

docs.title: Watch Sojourn in the Health Monitor
docs.text: The Health Monitor tab in the Sojourn app shows whether field tracking is working right now. It is separate from Sojourn Settings, so a support or operations group can watch Sojourn and fix its errors without changing its configuration.

docs.title: Who can open it
docs.text: Give people the Sojourn Health Monitor permission set; the Sojourn Admin permission set includes it. Without either, the tab says which permission set is needed and loads nothing. Health Monitor users can create the missing Interval, ignore, or resolve any error. Fixes that change configuration open Sojourn Settings, so for Health Monitor users without Sojourn Admin the page says "Ask a Sojourn admin" instead.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
• The banner reads Healthy, Needs attention, or Not working, with one line that says what needs you. Check again reads everything afresh.
  • Capture lists what stops Intervals being recorded: tracking off for the whole org, a Tracked object whose capture Flow is missing or cannot be read, a paused object or one waiting for Catch up, a failed backfill. On the Free plan, an object other than Case, Lead, and Opportunity shows "Plus plan needed" as information: it keeps its Intervals, and new changes are not recorded. If you cannot see Flows (you lack View Setup and Configuration and are not a Sojourn admin), an object captured by a Flow shows "Flow status hidden from you" as information: it does not change the overall status, and a Sojourn admin sees the real Flow status.
  • Jobs shows whether Live values, Reconcile, and Summaries are scheduled, their last run, and the next one. A job that is off shows as a warning until a Sojourn admin schedules it on the Sojourn Settings overview; on a new install, that includes Summaries. A job scheduled by a user who is no longer active shows as a failure, and Live values with an entry missing (for example after someone deleted one in Setup) shows as a warning with the minutes it still runs at; choosing the interval again on the overview restores it.
  • Errors counts the errors that need you, those in the last 24 hours, and those fixed in the last 24 hours, by type.
  • Recent errors lists the latest, each with its fix.

docs.title: Errors
docs.text:
The Errors tab lists Error Log rows by status, type, object, and age. Select rows to Create intervals, Mark resolved, or Ignore them together. The list shows the newest 200 errors that match the filters; when more match, it says "Showing the newest 200 errors" and Select all takes only those 200. Resolve or ignore them, or narrow the filters, to reach older ones. Open a row to see what happened, why, how to fix it, and the technical details for support.

Type What happened How to fix it Limit The save that changed the record was already close to a Salesforce governor limit, so Sojourn stepped aside to protect it. Choose Create interval, or leave it: the nightly reconcile retries Limit and DML errors older than an hour, up to three times. If many come from one import, pause the object before the next import and catch up after it. DML Salesforce refused to save the Interval, often because of a validation rule, a required field, or another app's trigger. Fix the cause the technical details name, then choose Create interval, or let reconcile retry it. Config A Tracked field names a field that was deleted or renamed, or that Sojourn can no longer read; or automation on an object changed a tracked field on every save, and Sojourn stopped following the saves three levels deep. In Sojourn Settings, remove the field or choose its replacement, then mark the error resolved. For the save loop, find the Flow or trigger on the named object that changes the field each time it saves, and stop it repeating. Business hours No usable business hours applied, so calendar minutes were recorded as business minutes. Choose default business hours in Sojourn Settings, or hours on the Tracked object, then mark the error resolved. Unknown Sojourn hit an error it did not expect. The user's save still went through. Choose Create interval. If it happens again, send the technical details to CloudAlgo support.

Create interval records the change at the time it happened and marks the error Resolved. It is refused when later changes to the same field were already recorded, because the change can no longer be placed; ignore the error, or run a History backfill to rebuild the record's history.

The same Create Interval action is on every Error Log record page.

You are done when

  • The banner reads Healthy, or every item it lists has a fix under way.
  • No error in the Errors tab reads Needs you without a reason you know.

docs.title: Before you install
docs.text: Check the edition, features, and permissions in Check the prerequisites. Sojourn installs on the Free plan; see Free and Plus plans.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
Release 1 is in development, so there is no AppExchange listing yet. Early access customers receive a package version ID from CloudAlgo. Request a package version ID.

  1. Install the package version, using the ID you were given:

    sf package install --package 04t... --target-org my-sandbox --wait 20

  2. Assign permission sets, as described in Assign permission sets.

  3. Decide who sees the dashboards. The four Sojourn dashboards run as the admin who installed Sojourn, and their folder is open to everyone, so every viewer sees what that admin sees, including the Case numbers, subjects, and owners that SLA Health and Desk Productivity list. Do one of these:
    • In Setup, open Dashboards, edit each Sojourn dashboard, and under View dashboard as choose a user whose access fits your viewers, or The dashboard viewer if your edition allows dynamic dashboards.
    • Or share the Sojourn Dashboards folder only with the people who may see that admin's data.
  4. Open the Sojourn app from the App Launcher.

You are done when

  • The Sojourn app appears in the App Launcher.
  • Each Sojourn dashboard runs as a user you chose, or its folder is shared only with the people who may see the installing admin's data.
  • The app opens with an Intervals tab in its navigation.

docs.title: Omni-Channel
docs.text: To record agent work from Omni-Channel, install the Sojourn Omni-Channel package after this one. It needs Omni-Channel turned on; this package does not. See Track agent work in Omni-Channel.

docs.title: Upgrade
docs.text: Install the new package version over the installed one, with the same command and the new ID. Intervals, settings, and scheduled jobs stay, and a later version never changes the packaged reports and dashboards you already have. Read the changelog first.

docs.title: Uninstall
docs.text: See Uninstall Sojourn: turn off the jobs first, and keep a copy of anything you need.

docs.title: Move settings from a sandbox
docs.text: Set Sojourn up once in a sandbox, then export the settings as a file and import them in production. See Move settings between orgs.

docs.title: Run the jobs
docs.text: Every Sojourn job runs as the admin who schedules or starts it, with that admin's access, and the Health Monitor shows each run. No job calls a service outside Salesforce. Schedule the jobs as a dedicated, long-lived Sojourn admin user rather than a person who may leave: if that user is deactivated, every run fails, and the Health Monitor says so and names the user.

docs.title: Scheduled jobs
docs.text:
Schedule them on the Jobs card of the Sojourn Settings overview: Turn on schedules a job, Change saves a new interval or time, and Turn off stops it. A run that is still going when the next one is due is skipped.

Job When What it does Plan Live values Every 10, 15, 20, 30, or 60 minutes Keeps minutes to date and breach flags current on open Intervals. On Plus, also writes the minute fields on records of objects with Write live values to the record on Free and Plus; the minute fields are Plus Reconcile Daily, at the time you choose Closes and flags Intervals of records that were deleted or merged, records values that changed without capture, and retries Limit and DML errors Free and Plus Summaries Daily, at the time you choose Counts closed Intervals into daily and monthly summary rows for reports. After it, purge runs when retention keeps a number of days Free and Plus; purge is Plus

Reconcile corrects Intervals that are open: a value that changed without capture closes the open Interval and opens the new value's. It never starts a field's first Interval, so a field with none, for example after a Fresh start, waits for its next change, and a blank field timed from its first value gets nothing until it has one.

docs.title: Jobs you start
docs.text:
Job Started from Plan Catch up Catch up on the Tracked objects list, after a pause Free and Plus Backfill The Backfill card on an object's screen; see Backfill past Intervals History and Seed are Plus; Fresh starts no job Purge now Purge now on Retention and purge; see Keep or purge Intervals Plus Rebuild summaries Rebuild on Retention and purge Free and Plus

One catch up, one backfill, and one purge run at a time across the org.

docs.title: Before you uninstall
docs.text: Turn off every scheduled job first, on the Jobs card. See Uninstall Sojourn.

docs.title: Move settings between orgs
docs.text: Set Sojourn up once in a sandbox, then move the settings to production, or to another sandbox, as a file.

docs.title: What the file carries
docs.text:
Tracked objects with their settings, Tracked fields, goals, queue business hours, Tracking enabled, and the default business hours. Retention is not in the file: production keeps what you chose there.

Business hours are written by name and queues by developer name, because record Ids differ between orgs.

docs.title: Export
docs.text: In the org you are copying from, open Sojourn Settings, then Data, then Export settings, and choose Export. Sojourn saves the file, named like sojourn-settings-2026-10-12.json, to your Files and opens it. Download it from the preview.

docs.title: Check the import
docs.text:
In the org you are copying to, open the same screen and choose Choose file. Sojourn reads the file and lists What the import will do: each Tracked object, Tracked field, goal, queue, and setting it will create, update, turn off, or skip, and why. Nothing has been changed yet.

  • An object or field this org does not have stops the whole import, and nothing is written. Add the field, or remove it from the source org, and export again.
  • A queue or business hours this org does not have is skipped, with the reason; the rest still imports.
  • A file that is not a Sojourn settings file, or is from a later format, is refused.

docs.title: Apply
docs.text:
Choose Apply. Everything in the list is written together, or nothing is.

Turn on Replace what is here before checking to make this org match the file: Tracked fields and goals that are not in the file are turned off. Nothing is deleted, and Tracked objects that are not in the file are left as they are.

You are done when

  • Choosing the same file again lists nothing to change.

docs.title: Track agent work in Omni-Channel
docs.text: Omni-Channel assigns work to agents without a normal save of the record, so a Case trigger never sees the assignment. The Sojourn Omni-Channel package reads Omni-Channel's own agent work and records one Interval per assignment: when the work is assigned or opened, and when it ends.

docs.title: Before you install
docs.text:
• The org is on the Plus plan. On the Free plan the package installs, but no agent work is recorded; see Free and Plus plans.

  • Omni-Channel is turned on in the org. The package reads Omni-Channel's agent work, which exists only when Omni-Channel is on; the core Sojourn package does not need it.

  • The core Sojourn package is installed, and the object the work belongs to, for example Case, is a Tracked object.

docs.title: Install
docs.text: Install the Sojourn Omni-Channel package version after the core package, with the ID you were given. It adds no tab, permission set, or setting screen.

docs.title: What it records
docs.text:
For each piece of work, Sojourn opens an Agent work Interval on the record with the agent as its value and its owner, and closes it with the business minutes when the work is closed, declined, canceled, transferred, or the agent becomes unavailable. One agent work Interval is open on a record at a time: a transfer closes the first agent's Interval and the next assignment opens a new one.

Agent work Intervals sit beside the record's other Intervals, with Tracked field set to Agent work and Source set to Omni-Channel. They take no Live values or goals, and do not count toward the 10 Tracked fields. Work on an object that is not tracked, or is paused, is not recorded, and a catch up does not replay it.

docs.title: Choose which statuses start the work
docs.text:
By default an Interval opens when the work is Assigned or Opened. To start only when the agent opens the work, set Omni Open Statuses in Setup, under Custom Settings, then Sojourn Settings, to Opened. Separate several statuses with commas.

You are done when

  • After an agent accepts and closes a routed Case, the Case's Intervals show one Agent work Interval with that agent and its business minutes.

docs.title: Assign permission sets
docs.text:
Sojourn ships five permission sets. Give each person the one that matches what they do.

Permission set Give it to What it allows Sojourn Admin Admins who configure tracking Create, edit, and delete all Sojourn records, including Tracked objects, Tracked fields, Goals, and queue business hours. Includes the Sojourn Admin custom permission. Sojourn Health Monitor A support or operations group Open the Health Monitor tab and act on errors: create the missing Interval, ignore, or resolve. Create, edit, and delete Intervals and Error Logs, with view and modify all, because repair closes other users' Intervals; read the configuration. No access to Sojourn Settings. A trusted role: assign it only to the people who maintain Sojourn's data. A repair it runs leaves the Case figures it cannot edit unchanged. Sojourn Manager People who report on intervals Read all intervals and interval summaries, and read Goals and tracking configuration. Sojourn User Everyone who should see intervals Read intervals, Goals, and Tracked objects, and the record timeline. Sojourn Site User Experience Cloud site users The record timeline on records they can open, and nothing else. It has no user license, so site users can hold it.

docs.title: Who sees which Intervals
docs.text:
Intervals are Public Read Only: anyone with a Sojourn permission set reads every Interval in reports and list views, including Intervals of records they cannot open. The record timeline shows a record's Intervals only to people who can open the record. Intervals hold only the values of the fields you chose to track, and the Sojourn User permission set has no access to the copied Opportunity amount or the snapshot fields.

To limit who reads Intervals, open Setup, then Sharing Settings, and set Interval to Private. Each person then sees the Intervals they own, which are the ones their own changes created, and those your sharing rules give them. Sojourn Manager and Sojourn Health Monitor include View All on Intervals, so people with them keep seeing every Interval. This setting governs reports and list views only: the record timeline follows the record's own sharing, so anyone who can open a record and has the Sojourn Timeline permission sees its full history there.

All five include the Sojourn Timeline permission, which the record timeline needs. The objects and rights each one grants are listed in Reference: Permission sets.

docs.title: Assign in Setup
docs.text:
1. In Setup, open Permission Sets.
  2. Select the permission set, then Manage Assignments, then Add Assignment.
  3. Choose the users and select Assign.

docs.title: Assign with the Salesforce CLI
docs.text:
sf org assign permset --name Admin --target-org my-sandbox

Often missed. Reports join intervals to Cases, Leads, and Opportunities. A manager also needs read access to those records to see them in a joined report.

You are done when

  • Each person has the Sojourn permission set for what they do; a Health Monitor user may also have Manager or User.
  • An admin sees the Sojourn Settings and Health Monitor tabs; a Health Monitor user sees the Health Monitor; a manager sees Intervals and Interval Summaries.

docs.title: Free and Plus plans
docs.text: Sojourn installs on the Free plan. The Plus plan adds tracking for any object, live minutes on the record, Backfill, the archive and purge, and Omni-Channel agent work. We switch an org to Plus from our License Management Org: nothing is reinstalled and no setting changes, and the switch reaches your org within a few minutes. To move an org to Plus, choose Upgrade to Plus on any Plus notice in Sojourn Settings, which opens CloudAlgo billing.

docs.title: What each plan includes
docs.text:
Capability Free Plus Tracking Case, Lead, and Opportunity, with their status, owner, and other fields Yes Yes Tracking any other object, custom or standard, through the capture Flow template No Yes Goals, breach flags, and business hours Yes Yes The record timeline, the 19 reports and 4 dashboards in Sojourn Yes Yes Pause, Catch up, and the nightly Reconcile and Summaries jobs Yes Yes Live values: minutes in the current status and with the current owner, written on the record No Yes Backfill with History or Seed No Yes Purge after a number of days, and the archive No Yes Omni-Channel agent work and the Agent Handle Time report, with the Sojourn Omni-Channel package No Yes The Health Monitor, and settings export and import Yes Yes

On the Free plan, the Live values job still runs: it keeps minutes to date and breach flags current on open Intervals of Case, Lead, and Opportunity. Backfill offers Fresh, which starts each record with its next change.

docs.title: In Sojourn Settings
docs.text: Plus features stay visible on the Free plan, with their controls off and a note that they are in the Plus plan, with an Upgrade to Plus link. The Add object dialog lists every object you could track and marks the ones that need Plus.

docs.title: When an org moves from Plus to Free
docs.text:
Nothing is deleted.

  • Intervals, summaries, and archived Intervals stay, and reports and the timeline keep showing them.
  • Objects other than Case, Lead, and Opportunity keep their configuration and their Intervals, but new changes on them are not recorded. The Tracked objects list marks each one "Plus plan: new changes are not recorded", the Health Monitor lists it as information, and Catch up waits until the org is on Plus again, keeping the pause window.
  • The live minute fields stop changing. Breach flags keep updating.
  • A Backfill or purge that is running stops at its next chunk. Purge stops deleting. The Retention screen shows your earlier choice, turned off, with the Plus notice.
  • Omni-Channel agent work is not recorded.

Moving back to Plus resumes all of it with no setup. Changes made while the org was on Free are not replayed.

docs.title: Edition and features
docs.text:
• Salesforce Enterprise, Unlimited, Performance, or Developer Edition, in Lightning Experience.
  • Professional Edition is not supported yet: Salesforce runs packaged Apex in Professional Edition only after a package passes its security review.
  • Business hours defined in Setup, under Business Hours. Sojourn uses the org default unless you set others.
  • For History backfill (Plus plan): Field History Tracking turned on for the fields you track, before the history you want to keep was written.
  • For Omni-Channel agent work (Plus plan): Omni-Channel turned on, and the Sojourn Omni-Channel package installed after Sojourn.
  • For the timeline on a site: an Experience Cloud site with authenticated members. Guest users cannot see it.

docs.title: People and permissions
docs.text:
• The person who installs needs the System Administrator profile, or the Download AppExchange Packages permission.
  • Admins who set Sojourn up need the Sojourn Admin permission set, and Customize Application to change the overview settings. See Assign permission sets.

docs.title: Storage
docs.text:
Each Interval is a record of about 2 KB in your data storage. When you pick Tracked fields, the object's screen estimates how many rows a month they add and what share of your storage that is a year. On the Plus plan, purge keeps storage in check on large orgs; see Keep or purge Intervals.

You are done when

  • Your org's edition is in the list above.
  • Setup lists at least one active business hours.

docs.title: Keep or purge Intervals
docs.text: Every change to a Tracked field adds an Interval, so a busy org collects millions of rows. Sojourn keeps the totals in summary rows and lets you decide how long the Intervals themselves stay.

docs.title: Summaries come first
docs.text:
Each night the Summaries job counts closed Intervals into daily and monthly summary rows: how many Intervals, how many records, and the total, average, shortest, and longest time, in business and calendar minutes, per object, field, value, owner, and period. Set its time on the Sojourn Settings Overview, under the jobs. Report on summaries with the Sojourn Interval Summaries report type; see the Report cookbook.

Summary rows are never purged with Intervals. Daily rows older than 400 days are removed after a complete purge run; monthly rows are kept.

docs.title: Choose retention
docs.text:
Purge and the archive are on the Plus plan. On the Free plan, every Interval is kept, and the screen shows Keep everything with a note; see Free and Plus plans.

Until you choose, the Sojourn Settings Overview shows Choose how long to keep Intervals. Open Sojourn Settings, then Data, then Retention and purge:

  • Keep everything: nothing is deleted. Reports read every Interval.
  • Keep N days, from 30 to 3,650: each night after Summaries, closed Intervals older than this are saved to a CSV file and deleted; their summaries are kept.

Choose Save retention. Keeping a number of days asks you to type DELETE first, because a purge deletes records. Days start and end at midnight in the org time zone.

docs.title: What a purge deletes
docs.text:
A purge deletes only Intervals that are closed, already summarised, and ended before the cutoff. Open Intervals are never deleted, however old.

It works 2,000 Intervals at a time, so a purge of a million Intervals leaves 500 CSV files on its run. Each part is first written to a CSV file, attached to the run's Purge Run record, then deleted in the same step: a part is saved and deleted together, or not at all. The first part that fails stops the run, and the run says why. Choosing Keep everything while a purge runs stops it at its next part, and the run says the rest is kept. Purge now waits while summaries are being built or rebuilt, because a rebuild still reads the Intervals a purge would delete.

The CSV file is your copy. Download it from the Purge Run record before you delete the record or the file. Sojourn never deletes them.

docs.title: The archive
docs.text: Turn on Also copy to the archive to keep each purged Interval in Sojourn's archive object as well, where it stays queryable. Your org includes 1 million archive records; more is a paid add-on from Salesforce. The CSV file is kept on every run either way.

docs.title: Purge now and the runs
docs.text:
Purge now starts a run straight away, without waiting for the night. The button is on only while the saved choice is Keep N days: on a new install, and under Keep everything, it is off. The confirmation names the window; type DELETE to confirm. One purge runs at a time; a second is refused with "A purge is already running. Try again when it finishes."

Purge runs lists each run: when it ran, its status (Queued, Running, Complete, or Failed), how many Intervals it deleted and archived, and how many files it holds; choose the files to open the run. A run counts its Intervals as each part finishes, so a run that stopped part-way shows what it deleted before it stopped. The run's record also keeps Interval Count: how many Intervals the run set out to delete when it started, so you can compare it with what it deleted.

docs.title: Rebuild summaries
docs.text:
Rebuild summaries recounts the summary rows of whole months from their Intervals, for example after a backfill. Choose From and To, then Rebuild. A rebuild is refused for a month a purge has cut into, because its deleted Intervals are no longer there to count, and for a range of more than 9,000 summary rows; rebuild fewer months at a time.

You are done when

  • The Overview no longer asks you to choose retention.
  • With Keep N days, the next morning's Purge Runs list shows a Complete run and its CSV file.

docs.title: Show the timeline on a record
docs.text: The Sojourn timeline shows how long a record spent in each value of its Tracked fields and with each owner: one lane per field, each stay as wide as its share of the time, with totals by value and by owner below.

docs.title: What it shows
docs.text:
• Lanes. One per Tracked field, the status field first and the owner last. Each stay is a segment sized by its business minutes, or calendar minutes when you switch to Calendar. The stay that is still open is Lantern orange and grows until it ends.
  • Goals. A stay with a Goal shows a tick where the goal fell; time past the goal is a red stripe along the bottom of the segment.
  • Details. Focus a segment with the keyboard or point at it to see its value, owner, when it began and ended, its business and calendar time, and its goal. Press Escape to close it.
  • Totals. Below the lanes, Time by value and Time by owner list each value's time, its share, and its number of stays.
  • History that was purged. When older Intervals were purged to the archive, the timeline also reads the archive and shows those stays dashed, marked as from the archive. Archived stays have no goal marks. See Keep or purge Intervals.
  • Up to date. The card keeps what it last read while the page is open; select Refresh to read the latest Intervals and the minutes so far.
  • Long histories. A record shows its newest 500 Intervals by default, at most 2,000; the timeline says so when older ones are left out. Reports show every Interval.

docs.title: Add it to a record page
docs.text:
1. Open a record of a Tracked object, then Setup (the gear), then Edit Page.
  2. Drag Sojourn Timeline from the Custom components into the page, for example the main column.
  3. Set its properties, then Save and Activate.
Property What it does Fields Tracked fields to show, as API names separated by commas; Owner shows the owner lane. Blank: all. Units Business hours or calendar time when the page opens. People can switch on the card. Most Intervals The newest Intervals shown, from 1 to 2,000. The default is 500. Show summary Show Time by value and Time by owner below the lanes.

docs.title: Who sees it
docs.text: People need the Sojourn Timeline permission, which the Sojourn User, Manager, Health Monitor, and Admin permission sets include; see Assign permission sets. The timeline shows the history of a record only to people who can open that record. Without the permission, the card says so and shows nothing else.

docs.title: Add it to an Experience Cloud page
docs.text:
1. In Experience Builder, open the record page for the object, for example Case Detail.
  2. Drag Sojourn Timeline onto the page and set its properties. To show customers no agent names, set Fields to the status field only, for example Status, and turn off Show summary; tooltips then name no owner either.
  3. Publish the site.
  4. Give site users the Sojourn Site User permission set. It has no user license, so site users can hold it, and it grants only the timeline.

Signed-in site users see the history of records they can open. Guest users are not supported.

Often missed. A site user sees a record's history only if they can open the record itself, through the site's sharing sets or sharing. Sojourn does not share records.

docs.title: When the card is empty
docs.text:
The card says What to do Intervals for this object appear once Sojourn tracks it Track the object in Sojourn Settings; a Sojourn admin sees a link there. The object is tracked through a Flow that is not active Turn the object's capture Flow on; see Track an object. No Intervals yet The first one starts when a Tracked field gets a value or changes. You need the Sojourn Timeline permission Assign a Sojourn permission set that includes it. This record is not shared with you Its history is hidden, as the record is. The timeline shows here on a record page It is placed outside a record page, as in a page builder before a record is chosen; it reads nothing there.

You are done when

  • A record page shows the timeline with a lane for each Tracked field, and focusing a segment shows its details.
  • A person without a Sojourn permission set sees the permission message instead of any history.

docs.title: Track an object
docs.text: You set up tracking in the Sojourn Settings tab of the Sojourn app. The page has a Sojourn menu on the left, in three sections: Capture (Overview, Tracked objects), Time (Business hours, Goals), and Data (Retention and purge, Export settings). Choose Collapse menu at its foot to fold it into icons; Sojourn remembers the choice in your browser. The tab needs the Sojourn Admin permission set; without it the page says so and shows nothing else. Changing the overview settings also needs the Customize Application permission, which system administrators have.

docs.title: Add an object
docs.text:
Case, Lead, and Opportunity are tracked on every plan; for the quickest start, see Track Cases and open your first report. Every other object, custom or standard, is on the Plus plan and needs a capture Flow; see Free and Plus plans.

  1. Open the Sojourn app and the Sojourn Settings tab, then Tracked objects in the menu.
  2. Choose Add object, search for the object, pick it, and choose Add object again. The list shows only objects Sojourn can track, so you never type an API name; objects you already track are marked Already tracked.
  3. On the object's screen, check the Tracked fields whose time in each value you want; they appear in the table beside the checkboxes, where Remove takes one off and Business hours sets hours for that field alone (leave it on Use the object's to use the object's hours). Picklists, lookups, checkboxes, dates, and short text fields are offered; formulas, auto-numbers, and long text are not.
  4. Leave Track owner on to measure time with each user and each queue.
  5. Choose Save.

Track only fields that everyone who reads Intervals may see. Sojourn copies a Tracked field's values into each Interval whatever the field-level security of the person who saved the record, and Sojourn User and Sojourn Site User can read those values, so a field you hide from a group shows to that group through Intervals and the timeline.

An object can have up to 10 Tracked fields, the owner included. From the sixth, the picker reminds you that each field adds Interval rows for every record; at 10, it asks you to turn one off first. Short text fields are listed apart, under "Usually not useful for time in value".

Each Tracked field has Start timing at the first value, on by default. When a record is created with the field blank, timing starts when the field first gets a value, so reports do not count the blank stretch before anyone filled it in. Turn it off to time the blank value from creation as well. The owner always starts at creation. Once a field has had a value, clearing it is a change like any other: the stay in the old value closes and a blank Interval opens, so time spent blank after a value is measured whichever way the switch is set.

Under the picker, the Estimate shows about how many Interval rows a month your choice adds, and how much of your data storage a year that is. It counts the records you can see that were created in the last 30 days and their field history; fields without history are assumed to change once a month. "At least" means the count reached its limit, so the real number is higher.

docs.title: Settings on the object's screen
docs.text:
• Status field and Closed values: the main status field and the values that mean the record is closed.
  • Name field: the field shown as the record's name on each Interval.
  • Business hours, or Business hours from a record field: the hours used for this object's business minutes.
  • Snapshot fields: up to 5 fields copied onto each Interval, for grouping reports by values such as priority.
  • Record types: track only these record types; leave empty for all.
  • Live values and its two minute fields: number fields on the record for the minutes in the current status and with the current owner. The Live values job keeps them current on the schedule set on the Jobs card of the Sojourn Settings overview (see Live values and the jobs).

docs.title: Check that capture is live
docs.text:
Each Tracked object shows a pill:

Pill Meaning Tracked by package Case, Lead, and Opportunity: Sojourn's own triggers capture every change. Flow active An active Sojourn capture Flow runs on this object. Flow missing No capture Flow runs yet. Follow the steps on the object's screen. Flow unknown Sojourn could not read your Flows, usually because you lack View Setup and Configuration. Paused Capture is paused for a bulk import. Inactive The object is configured but not tracked.

While an object's pill reads Flow missing or Flow unknown, its screen leads with four steps, and its fields and settings show as summaries until you choose Edit fields or Edit settings. On the Tracked objects list, Set up Flow opens those steps and Re-check Flows checks every object at once:

  1. In Setup, open Flows and the Sojourn Capture Template, then choose Save As, a new Flow. Keep "Sojourn" in the label.
  2. On the Start element, choose your object.
  3. In Sojourn: Capture Change, set the object for Record and Prior record to the same object. Pass the prior record on every save, as the template does: when some saves in one batch pass it and others do not, Sojourn records each correctly but in two passes, at twice the queries.
  4. Activate the Flow, then choose Re-check on the object's screen. The pill turns to Flow active.

Keep your copy a record-triggered Flow that runs after the save, as the template is: it runs in system context, so it records every user's changes. If you call Sojourn: Capture Change from a screen Flow or another Flow that runs as the user, give those users access to the action's Apex class (ChangeCapture) through a permission set of your own; only Sojourn Admin includes it, and without it the Flow fails for everyone else.

If both a trigger and a Flow capture the same change in one save, Sojourn records it once. Each Interval records how the change arrived in its Source field: Trigger, Flow, or Catch-Up.

Often missed. Setup objects such as User and Group cannot be tracked. Salesforce does not allow their changes and Sojourn's Intervals to be saved in one transaction, so Sojourn leaves them out of the list.

docs.title: Pause capture during a bulk import
docs.text:
The Tracked objects list shows each object's Tracked fields, whether it tracks the owner, its capture pill, and where its business hours come from: named hours, From record field, or Sojourn default.

Choose Pause on the Tracked object, in the list or on its screen, before a large import or update, and Resume afterwards. The list shows when the pause started. To stop tracking an object, turn off Active on its screen and choose Save; Turn on in the list brings it back. While paused, triggers and Flows skip the object, so the import runs without Sojourn's work. After you resume, the list says "Changes made while paused wait for Catch up". Choose Catch up to replay the records changed during the pause: each gets its Interval at the time it changed (its last modification, or its creation if it was created during the pause), and values Sojourn already holds are skipped, so running it twice is safe. A field with no open Interval gets its first one only on a record created during the pause; on older records it waits for the field's next change, and a blank field timed from its first value gets nothing until it has one. One catch up runs at a time across all objects: while one is going, the list says "Catch up is running" in place of the button, and starting another is refused. If part of the run is skipped or fails (for example, tracking was turned off, or the Error Log records a Limit or DML error), the list keeps offering Catch up, so you can run it again. If you pause the object while a catch up runs, even briefly and resumed before it ends, the pause window is kept for the next catch up. Pausing again before you catch up keeps the earlier start, so one catch up covers both pauses. The result of the last catch up is kept in the Tracked object record's Catch Up Message field, apart from the last backfill result, so a catch up never hides how the backfill went; the object's screen lists both in its Backfill card, as Last backfill and Last Catch up.

docs.title: Backfill past Intervals
docs.text: A new object starts with the next change. To give existing records their Intervals, use the Backfill card on the object's screen; see Backfill past Intervals.

docs.title: Live values and the jobs
docs.text: The Jobs card on the overview schedules Live values, Reconcile, and Summaries. See Run the jobs for when each runs and what it does.

docs.title: Business hours for each Interval
docs.text:
Sojourn uses the first of these that is set:

  1. The Tracked field's business hours.
  2. A business hours field on the record, chosen in Business hours from a record field.
  3. The queue's entry in Queue Business Hours, while a queue owns the record.
  4. The Tracked object's business hours.
  5. The default on the Sojourn Settings overview.
  6. The org default business hours.

If none applies, or the chosen business hours no longer exist, the Interval gets calendar minutes as business minutes, and an Error Log row of type BusinessHours tells you which setting to fix.

docs.title: The Error Log
docs.text:
Sojourn never fails your users' saves. If it cannot record a change, it writes an Error Log row instead; the overview shows how many are open and opens the Health Monitor, which explains each error and fixes it. See Watch Sojourn in the Health Monitor. To stop all capture at once, turn off Tracking enabled on the overview and choose Save settings.

You are done when the object's pill reads Tracked by package or Flow active, and changing a Tracked field on a record opens a new Interval for it and closes the previous one.

docs.title: Track Cases and open your first report
docs.text: Case, Lead, and Opportunity are tracked by the package's own triggers, on every plan, so they need no Flow.

docs.title: Track Cases
docs.text:
1. Open the Sojourn app, the Sojourn Settings tab, then Tracked objects in the menu.
  2. Choose Add object, search for Case, pick it, and choose Add object again.
  3. On the Case screen, check Status, and any other field whose time in each value you want, such as Priority.
  4. Leave Track owner on to measure time with each user and each queue.
  5. Under Status field, keep Status, and add Closed to Closed values.
  6. Choose Save.

docs.title: Cases and Leads routed by assignment rules
docs.text:
When an assignment rule routes a new Case or Lead, for example from Email-to-Case, Web-to-Case, Web-to-Lead, or an import that uses the default rule, Sojourn records the owner the rule chose as the record's first owner, from the moment the record was created. Salesforce runs assignment rules after the save that creates the record, in the same transaction, and Sojourn treats an owner set there as part of creating the record:

  • the first Owner Interval names the queue or user the rule chose, not the user who created the record (for Email-to-Case, the Automated Case User);
  • the first Status Interval names that owner too;
  • the Case's Owner Change Count does not count the routing.

An owner change in any later save, by a person, a Flow, or a rule run on edit, closes the Owner Interval and opens the next one as usual.

docs.title: Turn on the jobs
docs.text: On the Overview, the Jobs card schedules the three jobs that keep Intervals current. Choose Turn on for Live values, Reconcile, and Summaries. See Run the jobs for what each does.

docs.title: Open your first report
docs.text:
1. Change the status of a Case.
  2. Open the Reports tab and the Sojourn Reports folder.
  3. Open Time in Status by Case. The Case appears with its time in each status, in business hours.

You are done when

  • The Case's Intervals tab lists one Interval for each status it has had.
  • Time in Status by Case shows the Case with the time in its earlier status.

Other objects, custom or standard, are tracked through a capture Flow on the Plus plan; see Track an object.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Start with the Health Monitor: it checks capture, the jobs, and the Error Log, and says how to fix each problem it finds.

docs.title: A change made no Interval
docs.text: Check Fix Tracking enabled is off on the Sojourn Settings overview Turn it on. Reconcile records the values that changed meanwhile The object is paused or inactive Resume or Turn on it on the Tracked objects list, then Catch up The field is not a Tracked field Check it on the object's screen and choose Save; capture starts with the next change The object's pill reads Flow missing or Flow unknown Activate its capture Flow, as the object's screen shows; see Track an object The Health Monitor shows "Plus plan needed" for the object Objects other than Case, Lead, and Opportunity need the Plus plan; see Free and Plus plans The record type is not in Record types Add it, or leave the list empty to track every record type The Error Log has a Limit or DML row for the change Create interval on the error recreates it; Reconcile also retries it each night

docs.title: A report is empty or out of date
docs.text:
• Reports on Interval Summaries read the summary rows, which the Summaries job writes each night. Turn it on, or choose Rebuild on Retention and purge for past months.
  • Reports read only the Intervals and records you can see. Check the report runs as a user with the Sojourn Manager or Sojourn User permission set.
  • A report that runs past 10 minutes stops; filter it to fewer records or days. See Reports at large volume.

docs.title: The timeline is empty
docs.text: The timeline says why in its empty state: the object is not tracked, its Flow is not active, the record has no Intervals yet, you lack the Sojourn Timeline permission, or the record is not shared with you. See Show the timeline on a record.

docs.title: A backfill failed
docs.text: History backfill needs Field History Tracking on the fields. The Health Monitor names the error; choose Seed or Fresh instead, or turn on history and run it again. History and Seed are on the Plus plan.

docs.title: Uninstall Sojourn
docs.text: Uninstalling deletes every Sojourn object and its records: Intervals, summaries, Tracked objects, goals, the Error Log, and the archive. It also deletes the permission sets, reports, and dashboards that came with the package. Records outside Sojourn, such as your Cases, are not changed. The CSV files that purge saved are Salesforce Files owned by the admin who ran purge; they stay after the uninstall.

docs.title: Before you uninstall
docs.text:
1. On the Sojourn Settings overview, Turn off each job on the Jobs card: Live values, Reconcile, and Summaries.
  2. Wait for any Backfill, Catch up, or purge that is running to finish; the Health Monitor shows them.
  3. To keep the configuration, export it from Export settings; see Move settings between orgs.
  4. Remove the Sojourn permission sets from every user: in Setup, open Permission Sets, then each Sojourn set, then Manage Assignments. Salesforce refuses the uninstall while one is assigned.
  5. Remove anything you built on Sojourn's objects outside the package, such as your own reports, Flows, or fields on the Interval object. Salesforce refuses an uninstall while another component refers to a package component.

docs.title: Uninstall
docs.text:
1. If Sojourn Omni-Channel is installed, uninstall it first.
  2. In Setup, open Installed Packages, choose Uninstall next to Sojourn, and confirm.
  3. To keep the data, choose to save a copy of the package's data before it is deleted. Salesforce emails a link when the uninstall finishes; the export files are deleted two days after that.

You are done when

  • Installed Packages no longer lists Sojourn.
  • Scheduled Jobs in Setup lists no Sojourn job.
